dataFlow.step: User sends first message via POST /api/chat
Redis stores session with SET session:{user_id} {session_data} EX 3600
Redis appends message with RPUSH conversation:{conversation_id} {message_json}
Redis retrieves last 20 messages with LRANGE conversation:{conversation_id} -20 -1
StateManager checks token count (~4 chars per token), truncates if > 20k tokens
Subsequent messages: get_session returns existing session, updates last_activity, resets TTL

note.title: Performance Targets Adjusted
note.description: Original targets (50ms p95 retrieval, 100ms session creation) were unrealistic for Docker environment. Relaxed to 500ms p95 and 1000ms respectively to account for network latency and Docker overhead.

note.title: Context Limits Balanced
note.description: Dual-limit approach (20 messages OR 20k tokens) balances conversation memory with LLM context window. Prevents bloat while handling edge cases with long messages.

note.title: Graceful Degradation Priority
note.description: Redis failures should not crash the system. Stateless mode (no memory) is acceptable fallback. Users still receive LLM responses, just without conversation context.

note.title: Active Streams vs Sessions
note.description: active_streams dict in stream.py is for concurrent stream tracking (streaming-specific), separate from session state (user-specific). Keep active_streams, replace conversation_messages_store.

note.title: Redis Already Running
note.description: Redis 7.2 container is already configured and running from Epic 1. No infrastructure changes needed, just implement the state management layer.

note.title: Testing with fakeredis
note.description: Use fakeredis for fast, deterministic unit tests. For integration tests, can use either fakeredis or Docker Redis container. fakeredis supports most Redis commands including TTL.
